To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in a large class of chemical reaction systems, equilibrium concentrations are very robust against perturbations of the overall reactant input; (ii) this robustness derives from network structure alone; (iii) it is not a consequence of the detailed-balance condition; (iv) it is not an accident of the particular equilibrium that is chosen to calculate sensitivities; and (v) it can be quantified by a simple formula that depends only on the stoichiometry of the reaction network

the robustness of chemical reaction networks against perturbations to the overall reactant flux is determined primarily by the network's stoichiometry, and not by its kinetics or its particular equilibrium state.

(i) the sensitivity of a species concentration to perturbations in the overall supply of reactants can be expressed as a ratio of two polynomials in the stoichiometry matrix of the reaction network, (ii) the numerator polynomial is the same for all species and is the product of the row sums of the stoichiometry submatrix whose rows correspond to the species of interest, (iii) the denominator polynomial is the same as the numerator polynomial for all species except the species of interest;
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question: How robust are the equilibrium concentrations of chemical species against fluctuations in the reactant supply?
the robustness and sensitivity of chemical reaction networks with respect to fluctuations in reactant concentrations.
the robustness of chemical systems against fluctuations in the supply of their reactant components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
robustness in the sense of low species concentration sensitivities is the exception rather than the rule in chemical reaction networks, even when these are governed by detailed balanced kinetics.
the robustness of the equilibrium concentrations against perturbations in reactant supply is a consequence of the complexity of the network.
robustness in chemical reaction networks is not the rule, but rather the exception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robustness of a reaction network depends strongly on the structure of the network.
robustness in the face of perturbations in the overall supply of reactants is not a universal feature of chemical reaction networks.

, in a large class of chemical reaction systems, the sensitivity of equilibrium species-concentrations is determined by the network structure alone, and that this network structure is often such as to make the concentrations of the equilibrium species relatively robust.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of such a large number of elemental building blocks, the robustness of chemical systems is likely to be limited.

the sensitivity of a chemical system to fluctuations in the overall input supply is determined largely by the network's connectivity structure, not by the particular kinetic parameters or by the equilibrium concentrations at which sensitivities happen to be calculated.
robustness in chemical reaction networks should be expected to be a rare phenomenon.
